source: NCERT Class VII, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, History Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. The Second Urbanisation (c. 6th century BCE)
points: After the Harappan cities declined, cities rose again in the **Ganga plains** from about the **6th century BCE** — the **Second Urbanisation**.
Made possible by **iron tools** (clearing forests, better ploughs), **surplus agriculture** (especially **paddy/rice** transplantation), and growing **trade**.
**Punch-marked coins** (silver/copper) appeared; a fine pottery, **Northern Black Polished Ware (NBPW)**, marks these cities.
The script **Brahmi** came into use for writing.

sections.heading: 2. Janapadas and Mahajanapadas
points: A **janapada** = 'land where a people (jana) sets its foot' — an early territory/state.
By the 6th century BCE there were **sixteen mahajanapadas** ('great janapadas') across north India (e.g. **Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, Avanti, Vajji, Gandhara**).
Each had a **fortified capital** and needed **taxes, an army and officials**.

sections.heading: 3. Monarchies and Republics
points: Two kinds of states existed:

sub: **Ganas / Sanghas (republics/oligarchies)** — ruled by an **assembly of many chiefs/rajas**, e.g. the **Vajji sangha** (capital **Vaishali**).

points: **Mahavira** and **Gautama Buddha** belonged to gana-sangha families.

sections.heading: 4. Magadha — The Most Powerful
points: **Magadha** (in present-day **Bihar**) became the strongest mahajanapada.
Advantages: **fertile land**, **iron mines**, **elephants** from forests, and the **Ganga** for cheap transport.
Kings: **Bimbisara** and **Ajatashatru**; capital first **Rajagriha (Rajgir)**, later **Pataliputra (Patna)**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Second urbanisation = Ganga plains, c. 6th century BCE; based on iron + surplus paddy + trade.
Marker pottery = NBPW; earliest coins = punch-marked; script = Brahmi.
16 mahajanapadas; ganas/sanghas = republics (Vajji, capital Vaishali).
Magadha = most powerful (fertile land, iron, elephants, Ganga); kings Bimbisara & Ajatashatru.
Capitals of Magadha: Rajagriha → Pataliputra.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: There were **sixteen (16)** mahajanapadas.
**Ganas/sanghas** were **republics/oligarchies** (rule by many), not monarchies — Vajji is the key example.
**Magadha** (Bihar) — not Kosala — became the most powerful state.
**NBPW** pottery and **punch-marked** coins are markers of this age.
